judged_text: In sharing mode parseRefreshTokenResponse strips the zoom response to {access_token} plus the injected sentinel refresh_token:"refresh_token", and this stripped result is persisted as the credential key. The stored zoom credential loses token_type, scope and expires_in and carries a junk refresh token; if sharing is disabled or the endpoint removed, zoom refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and the integration fails permanently until the user reinstalls the app.

adjudication.rationale: In sharing mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` intentionally parses OAuth refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (only `access_token` plus a very limited set of other fields) and then *injects* `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it’s missing (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). Call sites then use this parsed output to update persisted credentials (e.g. Office365 merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and writes it back to Prisma; Google writes `key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` into Prisma). This can overwrite a real refresh token with the sentinel value and/or drop other token fields, creating persistent credential corruption consistent with the finding’s “junk refresh token / stripped fields” concern (even if the exact set of fields stripped depends on the schema).
